title: The scorpioid cyme traces a true logarithmic spiral

fields.label: Label
fields.value: The scorpioid cyme traces a true logarithmic spiral

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In a scorpioid cyme, where each shoot arises from the last on the same side at an equal angle and successive shoots diminish in length in a constant ratio, the shoots are tangents to a true logarithmic spiral; in the helicoid cyme the same spiral is present but hidden by a superimposed twist.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: successive shoots l_{n+1} = q\,l_n at equal angles are tangents to r = a e^{\theta\cot\alpha}

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The result is that the successive shoots, or successive increments of growth, are tangents to a curve, and this curve is a true logarithmic spiral.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XI, “The Logarithmic Spiral”; topic “Cymose inflorescences”. Scope: scorpioid and helicoid (cymose) inflorescences, e.g. borage

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: successive shoots l_{n+1} = q\,l_n at equal angles are tangents to r = a e^{\theta\cot\alpha}

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch11-04: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.73

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The mathematical conditions and curve fit are explicit. Public imagery can test visible scorpioid examples, while reliable 3D data for hidden helicoid geometry and representative taxonomic coverage are limited.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Digitize shoot origins, angles and lengths in scorpioid and helicoid cymes and test constancy of angle and length ratio, then fit the shoot tangents to logarithmic versus alternative spirals. Three-dimensional reconstruction can remove the superimposed helicoid twist.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Photographs often have perspective distortion and hidden shoots.

Successive lengths may vary with flowering stage and environment.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The scorpioid prediction is a concrete length-and-angle pattern, and herbarium photographs of the relevant families are public in large numbers. They are 2D and flattened, so they can test the scorpioid tangent spiral and not the claim that a helicoid cyme hides the same curve. Digitizing a sample is feasible but is compilation rather than a ready-made analysis.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On scorpioid cymes, measure successive shoot lengths and divergence angles and test whether the shoots are tangents to a logarithmic spiral. A constant length ratio and equal angles support it; varying ratios that miss the spiral refute it. The helicoid case additionally requires recovering a spiral after removing the twist.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Shoot lengths are not pre-measured; each inflorescence has to be digitized from a photograph.

Pressed specimens flatten the helicoid twist, so the hidden spiral is not recoverable from a typical sheet.
